cards.explanation: The answer is only the high priest. Only he goes through that second curtain. The other priests handle the first room, where the lampstand, the table and the consecrated bread are. The second room, the Most Holy Place, is his alone. That's a very short guest list, friends.

The answer is blood. The writer says the high priest never entered without it, and he offered it for himself and for the sins the people had committed in ignorance (Hebrews 9:7). He didn't just show up and hope for the best. Only the high priest went into that second room, and only once a year.

The answer is True, and notice who's doing the showing: the Holy Spirit. The writer says that by this arrangement, the way into the Most Holy Place had not yet been disclosed as long as the first tabernacle was still standing. So the tabernacle itself was showing something. I think that's worth a second look, friends.

The answer is that they couldn't cleanse the conscience. The writer says the gifts and sacrifices were unable to cleanse the conscience of the worshiper. They dealt with outside things, but the inside was still waiting. Keep that one in your apron pocket, friends, because it comes back in a big way later in this passage.

The answer is False. The writer says these were external regulations imposed until the time of reform. A rule that's imposed until a certain time has an end date. So they weren't meant to stay in place forever.

The answer is a greater one not made by hands. The writer says Christ went through the greater and more perfect tabernacle, one that is not made by hands and is not a part of this creation, as high priest of the good things that have come. Quite a contrast with the earthly sanctuary in verse 1, friends.

The answer is by His own blood. The writer says Christ did not enter by the blood of goats and calves, but entered the Most Holy Place once for all by His own blood, thus securing eternal redemption. That's the big contrast with the high priest, who offered blood for himself and for the people (Hebrews 9:7). Christ entered by His own.
The answer is False. The high priest went in once a year, but Christ entered the Most Holy Place once for all by His own blood. One entry, and redemption secured. No yearly schedule needed, bakers.

The answer is eternal. The writer says Christ entered once for all by His own blood, thus securing eternal redemption. The high priest went in once a year, but Christ entered once for all. That's the redemption He secured, friends.

The answer is Christ Himself. The writer says that through the eternal Spirit, He offered Himself unblemished to God. He is the one who offered, and He offered Himself. That's why His blood can purify our consciences from works of death, so that we may serve the living God.

The answer is True. The writer says the blood of Christ will purify our consciences from works of death, so that we may serve the living God. It cleans us on the inside, and it points us toward serving. Compare that to the old gifts, friends, which couldn't do this.
